messages:
anya: Heads-up — started a dry run of the large-scale KMS key rotation tool against a subset of customer envelopes this morning. Seeing sustained 429s from AWS KMS and a spike in our `envelope.rotate.errors` metric.

mike: Thanks for the ping. Do we have a per-key or per-account throttling metric? 429s could be due to hitting a single CMK rate limit.

anya: We pushed a dashboard: `kms.requests` by CMK id and `kms.errors.429`. Looks like 75% of failures are concentrated on 3 CMKs tied to a couple enterprise accounts.

kevin: That matches what I expected. For high-volume accounts we should do per-cmk token buckets and also stagger start times. We also need a durable checkpoint per-queue worker so retries don't reprocess whole partitions.

sarah: Agree. Current worker writes progress to memory and S3 manifests — that's not safe. Recommend a small Postgres table `rotation_progress` with columns (cmk_id, partition, last_processed_id, status, retry_count).

anya: Can we include a sample backoff snippet? We hit tight 429 bursts and naive exponential made things worse.

mike: Use exponential backoff with jitter + leader election to coordinate restarts. Pseudo: ```
for item in partition:
  try:
    rewrap(item)
  except ThrottlingError:
    backoff = min(MAX, base * 2**attempt)
    sleep(random_between(backoff/2, backoff))
    mark_checkpoint(item)
    break  # yield to allow other workers to process
```

kevin: Also add a per-CMK in-memory rate limiter so workers for the same CMK share a token bucket. That prevents thundering herd. Token refill should be based on observed KMS success rate + safety margin.

rotations-bot: Automation note: when a CMK hits >10% 429 rate for 5m, the bot will tag the rotation job state `throttled` and notify #eng-oncall.

anya: On RBAC: we had a question from infra — do rotation workers need kms:GenerateDataKey* or just Decrypt/Encrypt? For envelope rewrap we currently `Decrypt` with old CMK and `Encrypt` with new CMK (GenerateDataKey used only during initial envelope creation).

mike: Correct. For re-encryption you need `kms:Decrypt` on the old key and `kms:Encrypt` on the new key (or `ReEncrypt` if available and granted). Avoid broader permissions. Add CloudTrail write-only audit role for the workers to minimize blast radius.

kevin: For cross-cloud (GCP/Azure) customers we need analogous permissions: `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` and `cryptoKeyVersions.encrypt` for GCP; Azure needs `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` on Key Vault. Document these in the ops runbook.

sarah: Audit logs — we observed some missing entries in CloudTrail for the failure window. Possibly because retries hit KMS throttle before an API call fully accepted. We should add internal audit events emitted by the worker before/after each attempt to ensure we have a record even if KMS doesn't log.

anya: Good point. Worker should emit `rotation.attempt` with payload: `{cmk_id, envelope_id, attempt_ts, outcome}` to our audit topic. Keep those logs immutable and tied to the customer id for compliance.

mike: For DLQ: define a policy. After N retries (configurable, default 7) move envelope to `rotation_dlq` with reason codes and minimal metadata (envelope_id, cmk_id, error, last_attempt_ts). Only a human or a special remediation job can touch DLQ items.

kevin: Also include a safe-preview mode where we only simulate KMS calls (no writes) and validate full throughput behavior. That helped catch our race where manifests were updated before KMS completed.

sarah: Telemetry: New metrics to add: `rotation.progress.per_cmk`, `rotation.latency.per_envelope`, `rotation.dlq.count`, `kms.429_rate.per_cmk`. Also export traces with spans for `decrypt` and `encrypt` calls so we can link to CloudTrail events.

anya: One odd failure pattern: sometimes DynamoDB checkpoint writes conflicted across AZs and caused some partitions to get reprocessed. Switched to advisory locks on Postgres and that removed duplicates.

sec-oncall: For incident response, if we see global surge in 429s we should have an auto-fallback to pause non-critical rotations (flag in config `rotation.priority`) and throttle to <20 TPS per region until ops investigates.

mike: Ops playbook outline: 1) Pause low-priority jobs 2) Identify top CMKs causing 429s 3) If customer-caused, coordinate with AE and provide status 4) If system-caused, scale down workers + enable longer backoff + open ticket with cloud provider.

anya: Question: can we use KMS re-encrypt API to avoid decrypt/encrypt client-side for AWS? That would reduce network hops and possibly drop quota usage.

kevin: AWS `ReEncrypt` helps, but it still counts against both source and destination CMK quotas in practice. Worth it for CPU/bandwidth savings but test for quota implications. For GCP/Azure similar server-side ops exist but have different rate limits.

rotations-bot: Reminder: upcoming maintenance window Fri 03:00 UTC — production rotation cohort will be paused automatically between 03:00-04:00 UTC.

anya: Next steps I’ll: 1) implement Postgres checkpoints + advisory locks 2) add per-CMK token bucket 3) emit worker audit events before KMS call 4) add DLQ with metadata. Will post PR later today.

mike: lgtm, please @sec-oncall once PR is up so we can review the incident/runbook changes. :thumbsup:

kevin: If anyone wants to pair on the token bucket implementation I can help — ping me.

sarah: I'll draft the IAM snippets and a short KB for GCP/Azure permission mappings and attach to the PR.

anya: Thanks all — will post status updates in this thread.

rotations-bot: Job note: dry-run results summary: 12k envelopes processed, 340 errors, 3 CMKs throttled, 120 DLQ entries. See dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/rotations/1768405123

anya: Got the summary. Filing a post-run action item list now.
